# Part 0: Cool Features of Plotting

## Grassy Area Chart Art 🌱

```r
# ref: https://www.r-graph-gallery.com/138-green-world-data-art/

library(ggplot2)
library(RColorBrewer)
ngroup=20
names=paste("G_",seq(1,ngroup),sep="")
DAT=data.frame()

for(i in seq(1:50)){
  data=data.frame( matrix(0, ngroup , 3))
  data[,1]=i
  data[,2]=sample(names, nrow(data))
  data[,3]=prop.table(sample(
    c(rep(0,100),
    c(1:ngroup)),
    nrow(data)))
  DAT=rbind(DAT,data)
}
colnames(DAT)=c("Year","Group","Value")
DAT=DAT[order( DAT$Year, DAT$Group) , ]

ggplot(DAT, aes(x=Year, y=Value, fill=Group )) + 
  geom_area(alpha=1 , color="transparent" )+
  theme_bw() +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette="greens", breaks=rev(levels(DAT$Group)))+
  theme(line = element_blank(),
        text = element_blank(),
       # line = element_blank(),
        title = element_blank(),
        legend.position="none",
        panel.border = element_blank(),
        panel.background = element_blank())

```

::: {.callout-tip icon="true"}

Read more about it at <a href="https://www.data-to-art.com/" target="_blank">*Data to Art*</a>

:::

# Part 1: Getting Started With `Plotly`


## What is Plotly? 🚀

::: {.callout-blue icon="false"}
**Plotly** is a powerful graphing library that creates interactive, publication-quality visualizations
:::

**Key Features:**

- **Interactive**: Hover for details, zoom, pan, download
- **Web-based and shareable**: Works in RStudio, R Markdown, and Shiny
- **Versatile**: 40+ chart types
- **Beautiful**: Professional styling out-of-the-box

**Plotly vs ggplot2:** ggplot2 excels at static graphics; Plotly adds interactivity for web dashboards and exploration.

---

## Clean Session Setup 🧹

::: {.callout-tip icon="true"}
**Start with a clean workspace** for reproducible R scripts
:::

```r
# Clear objects, plots, and console
remove_existing_objects <- function() {
  rm(list = ls())
  graphics.off()
  cat("\014")
}

remove_existing_objects()
```

---

## Install and Load Packages 📦

::: {.callout-note icon="false"}
List the packages your script needs, then install any that are missing.
:::

```r
required_packages <- c('plotly', 'dplyr', 'tidyverse')

install_and_load <- function(packages) {
  for(pkg in packages) {
    if(!require(pkg, character.only = TRUE, quietly = TRUE)) {
      install.packages(pkg)
      library(pkg, character.only = TRUE)
    }
  }
}

install_and_load(required_packages)
```

---

## Your First Plotly Plot 🎯

::: {.callout-note icon="false"}
**Simple Scatter Plot** — The easiest way to start with Plotly
:::

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false
library(plotly)

# Create a simple scatter plot
plot_ly(data = mtcars, 
        x = ~wt, 
        y = ~mpg, 
        type = 'scatter',
        mode = 'markers')
```

---

## Result: Your First Plot 🎯

```{r}
#| echo: false
ggplot(mtcars, aes(wt, mpg)) +
  geom_point(size = 3)
```

::: {.callout-note icon="false"}
Static ggplot2 version of the plotly output; run the plotly code for the interactive version.
:::

---

## Plotly Syntax: Key Components 🎯

::: {.callout-note icon="false"}
The first example uses the same core arguments in `plot_ly()`.
:::

- `plot_ly()`: Main plotting function
- `data`: Your data frame
- `x`, `y`: Variables (use `~` notation)
- `type`: Chart type ('scatter', 'bar', 'box', etc.)
- `mode`: For scatter plots ('markers', 'lines', 'markers+lines')

---

## Interactive Features 🖱️

::: {.callout-tip icon="true"}
Every Plotly plot comes with built-in interactivity!
:::

**Explore the plot:**

1. **Hover** to inspect data values
2. **Zoom** by clicking and dragging
3. **Pan** with Shift + drag
4. **Box or lasso select** points
5. **Reset** with a double-click

---

## Plotly Toolbar Controls 🖱️

- 📷 Download the plot as PNG
- 🔍 Zoom, pan, and select points
- 🏠 Reset axes to original view
- ⚙️ Toggle spike lines and axis hover

---

# Part 2: Scatter Plots

---

## Basic Scatter Plot 📊

::: {.callout-blue icon="false"}
**Exploring Relationships Between Variables**
:::

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false
library(plotly)

# Basic scatter plot
fig <- plot_ly(data = iris,
               x = ~Sepal.Length,
               y = ~Petal.Length,
               type = 'scatter',
               mode = 'markers')

fig
```

---

## Result: Basic Scatter Plot 📊

```{r}
#| echo: false
ggplot(iris, aes(Sepal.Length, Petal.Length)) +
  geom_point(size = 3)
```

---

## Customize Scatter Plot Markers 🎨

::: {.callout-tip icon="true"}
Adjust marker size, fill, and outline to make points easier to distinguish.
:::

**Customizing Markers:**

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false
# Add color, size, and opacity
fig <- plot_ly(data = iris,
               x = ~Sepal.Length,
               y = ~Petal.Length,
               type = 'scatter',
               mode = 'markers',
               marker = list(size = 10,
                           color = 'rgba(255, 182, 193, .9)',
                           line = list(color = 'rgba(152, 0, 0, .8)',
                                      width = 2)))
fig
```

---

## Result: Custom Markers 🎨

```{r}
#| echo: false
ggplot(iris, aes(Sepal.Length, Petal.Length)) +
  geom_point(size = 4, shape = 21, stroke = 1.2,
             fill = alpha("#FFB6C1", 0.9), color = "#980000")
```

---

## Color Points by Category 🎨

::: {.callout-note icon="false"}

### Adding Color Dimension
Visualize a third variable with color

:::

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false
fig <- plot_ly(iris, x = ~Sepal.Length, y = ~Petal.Length,
               color = ~Species, type = 'scatter', mode = 'markers')
fig
```

---

## Result: Color by Species 🎨

```{r}
#| echo: false
ggplot(iris, aes(Sepal.Length, Petal.Length, color = Species)) +
  geom_point(size = 3)
```

---

## Add Labels and Choose Colors 🎨

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false
fig <- fig %>% layout(
  title = "Iris Dataset: Sepal vs Petal Length",
  xaxis = list(title = "Sepal Length (cm)"),
  yaxis = list(title = "Petal Length (cm)")
)

fig
```

**Color Options:**

- `color = ~variable`: map a variable to color
- `colors = 'Set1'`: use an RColorBrewer palette
- `colors = c(...)`: provide custom colors

---

## Result: Labeled Scatter Plot 🏷️

```{r}
#| echo: false
ggplot(iris, aes(Sepal.Length, Petal.Length, color = Species)) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  labs(title = "Iris Dataset: Sepal vs Petal Length",
       x = "Sepal Length (cm)", y = "Petal Length (cm)")
```

---

## Scatter with Custom Hover 🔍

::: {.callout-tip icon="true"}
**Customize Tooltip Information**
:::

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false
# Custom hover text
fig <- plot_ly(data = iris,
               x = ~Sepal.Length,
               y = ~Petal.Length,
               color = ~Species,
               type = 'scatter',
               mode = 'markers',
               text = ~paste("Species:", Species,
                           "<br>Sepal Width:", Sepal.Width,
                           "<br>Petal Width:", Petal.Width),
               hoverinfo = 'text')

fig
```

---

## Choose What Appears on Hover 🔍

::: {.callout-note icon="false"}
Use `hoverinfo` to show only the details that help explain the plot.
:::

**Hover Options:**

- `hoverinfo = 'x'`: Show only x value
- `hoverinfo = 'y'`: Show only y value
- `hoverinfo = 'x+y'`: Show both coordinates
- `hoverinfo = 'text'`: Show custom text
- `hoverinfo = 'none'`: Disable hover

---

## Scatter with Trend Line 📈 {.smaller}

::: {.callout-blue icon="false"}
**Adding Statistical Models**
:::

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false
library(plotly)
library(dplyr)

# Calculate linear model
model <- lm(Petal.Length ~ Sepal.Length, data = iris)
iris$predicted <- predict(model)

# Plot with trend line
fig <- plot_ly(data = iris, x = ~Sepal.Length) %>%
  add_markers(y = ~Petal.Length, name = 'Actual',
              marker = list(size = 8, opacity = 0.6)) %>%
  add_lines(y = ~predicted, name = 'Trend',
            line = list(color = 'red', width = 2)) %>%
  layout(title = "Scatter Plot with Linear Regression",
         xaxis = list(title = "Sepal Length"),
         yaxis = list(title = "Petal Length"))

fig
```

---

## Result: Scatter with Trend Line 📈

```{r}
#| echo: false
ggplot(iris, aes(Sepal.Length, Petal.Length)) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5, alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, color = "red") +
  labs(title = "Scatter Plot with Linear Regression",
       x = "Sepal Length", y = "Petal Length")
```

---

# Part 3: Box Plots

---

## Basic Box Plot 📦

::: {.callout-note icon="false"}
**Visualizing Distributions** — Box plots show median, quartiles, and outliers
:::

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false
# Simple box plot
fig <- plot_ly(data = iris,
               y = ~Sepal.Length,
               type = 'box',
               name = 'Sepal Length')

fig
```

---

## Result: Basic Box Plot 📦

```{r}
#| echo: false
ggplot(iris, aes(x = "Sepal Length", y = Sepal.Length)) +
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.4) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Sepal.Length")
```

---

## Read a Box Plot 📦

::: {.callout-note icon="false"}
The box summarizes the distribution; points beyond the whiskers are outliers.
:::

- **Box**: Interquartile range (IQR) - middle 50% of data
- **Line in Box**: Median (50th percentile)
- **Whiskers**: Extend to 1.5 × IQR
- **Points**: Outliers beyond whiskers
- Hover to inspect exact values

---

## Grouped Box Plots 📊 {.smaller}

::: {.callout-blue icon="false"}
**Comparing Multiple Groups**
:::

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false
# Box plot by species
fig <- plot_ly(data = iris,
               y = ~Sepal.Length,
               x = ~Species,
               color = ~Species,
               type = 'box')

fig <- fig %>% layout(
  title = "Sepal Length Distribution by Species",
  xaxis = list(title = "Species"),
  yaxis = list(title = "Sepal Length (cm)")
)

fig
```

---

## Result: Grouped Box Plots 📊

```{r}
#| echo: false
ggplot(iris, aes(Species, Sepal.Length, fill = Species)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(title = "Sepal Length Distribution by Species",
       x = "Species", y = "Sepal Length (cm)")
```

---

## Show Individual Values on Box Plots 🔎

::: {.callout-tip icon="true"}
Jitter spreads points horizontally so overlapping observations are easier to see.
:::

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false
# Show points on box plot
fig <- plot_ly(data = iris,
               y = ~Sepal.Length,
               x = ~Species,
               color = ~Species,
               type = 'box',
               boxpoints = 'all',        # Show all points
               jitter = 0.3,             # Spread points horizontally
               pointpos = -1.8)          # Position of points

fig
```

---

## Result: Box Plot with Points 🔎

```{r}
#| echo: false
ggplot(iris, aes(Species, Sepal.Length, fill = Species)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA, alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.15, size = 2)
```

---

## Horizontal Box Plots 🔄 {.smaller}

::: {.callout-tip icon="true"}
**Better for Long Category Names**
:::

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false
# Horizontal orientation
fig <- plot_ly(data = iris,
               x = ~Sepal.Length,        # x for horizontal
               y = ~Species,             # y for categories
               color = ~Species,
               type = 'box',
               orientation = 'h')        # h for horizontal

fig <- fig %>% layout(
  title = "Sepal Length by Species (Horizontal)",
  xaxis = list(title = "Sepal Length (cm)"),
  yaxis = list(title = "")
)

fig
```

---

## Result: Horizontal Box Plots 🔄

```{r}
#| echo: false
ggplot(iris, aes(Sepal.Length, Species, fill = Species)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(title = "Sepal Length by Species (Horizontal)",
       x = "Sepal Length (cm)", y = NULL)
```

---

## Multiple Box Plots 📈 {.smaller}

::: {.callout-note icon="false"}
**Comparing Different Measurements**
:::

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false
# Create subplot with multiple box plots
fig <- plot_ly(data = iris, x = ~Species) %>%
  add_trace(y = ~Sepal.Length, name = 'Sepal Length',
            type = 'box', boxmean = 'sd') %>%
  add_trace(y = ~Sepal.Width, name = 'Sepal Width',
            type = 'box', boxmean = 'sd') %>%
  add_trace(y = ~Petal.Length, name = 'Petal Length',
            type = 'box', boxmean = 'sd') %>%
  add_trace(y = ~Petal.Width, name = 'Petal Width',
            type = 'box', boxmean = 'sd') %>%
  layout(title = "All Iris Measurements by Species",
         yaxis = list(title = "Measurement (cm)"))

fig
```

---

## Result: Multiple Box Plots 📈

```{r}
#| echo: false
iris |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-Species, names_to = "Measurement", values_to = "value") |>
  ggplot(aes(Species, value, fill = Measurement)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(title = "All Iris Measurements by Species", y = "Measurement (cm)")
```

---

## Show the Mean on a Box Plot 📈

::: {.callout-note icon="false"}
Set `boxmean = 'sd'` to show the mean and standard deviation.
:::

# Part 4: Histograms

---

## Basic Histogram 📊

::: {.callout-blue icon="false"}
**Distribution of a Single Variable**
:::

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false
# Simple histogram
fig <- plot_ly(x = ~iris$Sepal.Length,
               type = 'histogram',
               marker = list(color = 'steelblue',
                           line = list(color = 'white', width = 1)))

fig <- fig %>% layout(
  title = "Distribution of Sepal Length",
  xaxis = list(title = "Sepal Length (cm)"),
  yaxis = list(title = "Count")
)

fig
```

---

## Result: Basic Histogram 📊

```{r}
#| echo: false
ggplot(iris, aes(Sepal.Length)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 15, fill = "steelblue", color = "white") +
  labs(title = "Distribution of Sepal Length",
       x = "Sepal Length (cm)", y = "Count")
```

---

## Histogram Bin Controls 📊

::: {.callout-note icon="false"}
Choose the number of bins or specify exact bin boundaries.
:::

- `nbinsx`: Number of bins (auto-calculated if not specified)
- `xbins`: Manual bin configuration

---

## Understanding Binwidth ⚖️

::: {.callout-warning icon="true"}
**Binwidth Matters!** The choice of binwidth dramatically affects interpretation
:::

**Too Few Bins (Large Binwidth):**

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false
# Very few bins - loses detail
fig <- plot_ly(x = ~iris$Sepal.Length,
               type = 'histogram',
               nbinsx = 5)  # Only 5 bins
fig
```

**Advantages:** ✅ Clear overall pattern, less noise  
**Disadvantages:** ❌ Loses fine-grained patterns, may hide bimodality

---

## Result: 5 Bins 📊

```{r}
#| echo: false
ggplot(iris, aes(Sepal.Length)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 5, fill = "steelblue", color = "white")
```

---

## Binwidth: Finding Balance 🎯

**Too Many Bins (Small Binwidth):**

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false
# Too many bins - too noisy
fig <- plot_ly(x = ~iris$Sepal.Length,
               type = 'histogram',
               nbinsx = 50)  # 50 bins
fig
```

**Advantages:** ✅ Shows fine detail, reveals minor peaks  
**Disadvantages:** ❌ Noisy, harder to see overall pattern, sparse bins

---

## Result: 50 Bins 📊

```{r}
#| echo: false
ggplot(iris, aes(Sepal.Length)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 50, fill = "steelblue", color = "white")
```

---

## Choosing a Binwidth 🎨

::: {.callout-tip icon="true"}
**Rules of Thumb for Choosing Bins**
:::

**Common Rules:**

1. **Sturges' Rule**: `bins ≈ log₂(n) + 1`
2. **Square Root**: `bins ≈ √n`
3. **Scott's Rule**: `binwidth ≈ 3.5σ / ∛n`
4. **Freedman-Diaconis**: `binwidth ≈ 2IQR / ∛n`

---

## Try an Automatic Binwidth 🎨

::: {.callout-tip icon="true"}
Plotly chooses a default binning; compare it with other choices to see which best tells the data's story.
:::

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false
# Good balance - auto-calculated
fig <- plot_ly(x = ~iris$Sepal.Length,
               type = 'histogram',
               marker = list(color = 'lightgreen',
                           line = list(color = 'darkgreen', width = 1)))
fig  # Plotly uses smart defaults!
```

---

## Result: Automatic Binwidth 🎨

```{r}
#| echo: false
ggplot(iris, aes(Sepal.Length)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 15, fill = "lightgreen", color = "darkgreen")
```

---

## Custom Binwidth 🔧 {.smaller}

::: {.callout-note icon="false"}
**Manual Control Over Bins**
:::

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false
# Specify exact bin size
fig <- plot_ly(x = ~iris$Sepal.Length,
               type = 'histogram',
               xbins = list(
                 start = 4.0,     # First bin starts at 4
                 end = 8.0,       # Last bin ends at 8
                 size = 0.2       # Each bin is 0.2 cm wide
               ))

fig <- fig %>% layout(
  title = "Sepal Length with 0.2 cm Bins",
  xaxis = list(title = "Sepal Length (cm)"),
  yaxis = list(title = "Frequency")
)

fig
```

---

## Result: Custom Binwidth 🔧

```{r}
#| echo: false
ggplot(iris, aes(Sepal.Length)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.2, boundary = 4, fill = "steelblue", color = "white") +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(4, 8)) +
  labs(title = "Sepal Length with 0.2 cm Bins",
       x = "Sepal Length (cm)", y = "Frequency")
```

---

## Overlaid Histograms 📊 {.smaller}

::: {.callout-blue icon="false"}
**Comparing Distributions**
:::

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false
# Create separate data for each species
setosa <- iris %>% filter(Species == "setosa")
versicolor <- iris %>% filter(Species == "versicolor")
virginica <- iris %>% filter(Species == "virginica")

# Overlaid histograms
fig <- plot_ly(alpha = 0.6) %>%
  add_histogram(x = ~setosa$Sepal.Length, name = "Setosa") %>%
  add_histogram(x = ~versicolor$Sepal.Length, name = "Versicolor") %>%
  add_histogram(x = ~virginica$Sepal.Length, name = "Virginica") %>%
  layout(barmode = "overlay",          # Overlay instead of stack
         title = "Sepal Length by Species",
         xaxis = list(title = "Sepal Length (cm)"),
         yaxis = list(title = "Count"))

fig
```

**Other `barmode` options:** `'stack'`, `'group'`

---

## Result: Overlaid Histograms 📊

```{r}
#| echo: false
ggplot(iris, aes(Sepal.Length, fill = Species)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.2, alpha = 0.6, position = "identity") +
  labs(title = "Sepal Length by Species",
       x = "Sepal Length (cm)", y = "Count")
```

---

## Stacked Histograms 📚 {.smaller}

::: {.callout-tip icon="true"}
**Showing Composition**
:::

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false
# Stacked histogram
fig <- plot_ly() %>%
  add_histogram(x = ~setosa$Sepal.Length, 
                name = "Setosa",
                marker = list(color = '#e74c3c')) %>%
  add_histogram(x = ~versicolor$Sepal.Length,
                name = "Versicolor",
                marker = list(color = '#3498db')) %>%
  add_histogram(x = ~virginica$Sepal.Length,
                name = "Virginica",
                marker = list(color = '#2ecc71')) %>%
  layout(barmode = "stack",
         title = "Species Distribution Across Sepal Lengths",
         xaxis = list(title = "Sepal Length (cm)"),
         yaxis = list(title = "Total Count"))

fig
```

---

## Result: Stacked Histograms 📚

```{r}
#| echo: false
ggplot(iris, aes(Sepal.Length, fill = Species)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.2, position = "stack") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#e74c3c", "#3498db", "#2ecc71")) +
  labs(title = "Species Distribution Across Sepal Lengths",
       x = "Sepal Length (cm)", y = "Total Count")
```

---

# Part 5: Other Plot Types

---

## Bar Charts 📊 {.smaller}

::: {.callout-note icon="false"}
**Categorical Data Visualization**
:::

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false
# Count by species
species_count <- iris %>%
  group_by(Species) %>%
  summarise(Count = n())

fig <- plot_ly(data = species_count,
               x = ~Species,
               y = ~Count,
               type = 'bar',
               marker = list(color = c('#e74c3c', '#3498db', '#2ecc71')))

fig <- fig %>% layout(
  title = "Sample Count by Species",
  xaxis = list(title = "Species"),
  yaxis = list(title = "Number of Samples")
)

fig
```

## Violin Plots 🎻 {.smaller}

::: {.callout-tip icon="true"}

:::

```{r}
#| echo: true

               type = 'violin',

  xaxis = list(title = "Species"),

)

fig
```

```{r}
fig <- plot_ly(x = colnames(cor_matrix), y = rownames(cor_matrix),
               z = cor_matrix, type = "heatmap",
               colors = colorRamp(c("blue", "white", "red"))) %>%
  layout(title = "Iris Feature Correlation Matrix",
         xaxis = list(title = ""), yaxis = list(title = ""))
fig
```

```{r}

              color = ~Species, type = "scatter", mode = "markers")
p4 <- plot_ly(iris, x = ~Species, y = ~Sepal.Length,
              color = ~Species, type = "box")
```

```{=html}
<div id="plotly-generator" style="padding: 8px; border: 2px solid #9B59B6; border-radius: 8px; background: #f8f9fa; font-size: 0.65em; max-width: 900px; margin: 0 auto;">

      <label style="font-weight: bold; font-size: 0.85em;">Dataset:</label>

        <option value="box">Box Plot</option>
        <option value="histogram">Histogram</option>

        <option value="line">Line Chart</option>

        <option value="3d">3D Scatter</option>
      </select>
      
      <label style="font-weight: bold; margin-top: 3px; display: block; font-size: 0.85em;">Color By:</label>
      <select id="plotly-color" style="width: 100%; padding: 2px; margin: 2px 0; font-size: 0.9em;">
        <option value="none">None</option>
        <option value="Species">Species</option>
        <option value="Sepal.Width">Sepal.Width</option>
      </select>
      
      <label style="font-weight: bold; margin-top: 3px; display: block; font-size: 0.85em;">Color Scale:</label>
      <select id="plotly-colorscale" style="width: 100%; padding: 2px; margin: 2px 0; font-size: 0.9em;">
        <option value="default">Default</option>
        <option value="Viridis">Viridis</option>
        <option value="Blues">Blues</option>
        <option value="Reds">Reds</option>
        <option value="RdBu">RdBu</option>
      </select>

    <div style="display: flex; flex-direction: column; justify-content: space-around;">
      <label style="font-size: 0.9em;"><input type="checkbox" id="plotly-markers"> Show Markers</label>
      <label style="font-size: 0.9em;"><input type="checkbox" id="plotly-hover"> Custom Hover</label>
      <label style="font-size: 0.9em;"><input type="checkbox" id="plotly-title" checked> Add Title</label>
      <button id="generate-plotly-code" style="padding: 5px; background: #9B59B6; color: white; border: none; border-radius: 4px; cursor: pointer; font-weight: bold; font-size: 0.9em;">
        Generate Code
      </button>

  </div>
  
  <div style="background: #2c3e50; color: #ecf0f1; padding: 8px; border-radius: 4px; margin: 5px 0; font-family: 'Courier New', monospace; white-space: pre-wrap; font-size: 0.8em; max-height: 200px; overflow-y: auto; line-height: 1.2;">
<code id="plotly-generated-code">Click "Generate Code" to create your Plotly code!</code>
  </div>
  
  <button id="copy-plotly-code" style="padding: 4px 12px; background: #3498db; color: white; border: none; border-radius: 4px; cursor: pointer; font-size: 0.85em;">
    📋 Copy
  </button>
</div>

<script>
function updatePlotlyVariableOptions() {
  const dataset = document.getElementById('plotly-dataset').value;
  const xSelect = document.getElementById('plotly-x');
  const ySelect = document.getElementById('plotly-y');
  const colorSelect = document.getElementById('plotly-color');
  
  // Clear existing options
  xSelect.innerHTML = '';
  ySelect.innerHTML = '';
  colorSelect.innerHTML = '<option value="none">None</option>';
  
  let variables = [];
  let categoricalVar = '';
  
  if (dataset === 'iris') {
    variables = ['Sepal.Length', 'Sepal.Width', 'Petal.Length', 'Petal.Width'];
    categoricalVar = 'Species';
  } else if (dataset === 'mtcars') {
    variables = ['mpg', 'disp', 'hp', 'wt', 'qsec'];
    categoricalVar = 'cyl';
  }
  
  // Populate X and Y
  variables.forEach(v => {
    xSelect.innerHTML += `<option value="${v}">${v}</option>`;
    ySelect.innerHTML += `<option value="${v}">${v}</option>`;
  });
  
  // Set defaults
  xSelect.value = variables[0];
  ySelect.value = variables[2] || variables[1];
  
  // Add color options
  variables.forEach(v => {
    colorSelect.innerHTML += `<option value="${v}">${v}</option>`;
  });
  colorSelect.innerHTML += `<option value="${categoricalVar}">${categoricalVar}</option>`;
}

function generatePlotlyCode() {
  const dataset = document.getElementById('plotly-dataset').value;
  const xVar = document.getElementById('plotly-x').value;
  const yVar = document.getElementById('plotly-y').value;
  const plotType = document.getElementById('plotly-type').value;
  const colorVar = document.getElementById('plotly-color').value;
  const colorScale = document.getElementById('plotly-colorscale').value;
  const showMarkers = document.getElementById('plotly-markers').checked;
  const customHover = document.getElementById('plotly-hover').checked;
  const addTitle = document.getElementById('plotly-title').checked;
  
  let code = `library(tidyverse)\nlibrary(plotly)\n\n`;
  
  // Generate code based on plot type
  if (plotType === 'scatter') {
    code += `fig <- plot_ly(data = ${dataset},\n`;
    code += `               x = ~${xVar},\n`;
    code += `               y = ~${yVar},\n`;
    if (colorVar !== 'none') {
      code += `               color = ~${colorVar},\n`;
      if (colorScale !== 'default') {
        code += `               colors = '${colorScale}',\n`;
      }
    }
    code += `               type = 'scatter',\n`;
    code += `               mode = '${showMarkers ? 'markers' : 'markers'}',\n`;
    code += `               marker = list(size = 8))`;
    
  } else if (plotType === 'box') {
    code += `fig <- plot_ly(data = ${dataset},\n`;
    code += `               x = ~${colorVar !== 'none' ? colorVar : xVar},\n`;
    code += `               y = ~${yVar},\n`;
    if (colorVar !== 'none') {
      code += `               color = ~${colorVar},\n`;
    }
    code += `               type = 'box',\n`;
    code += `               boxpoints = 'outliers')`;
    
  } else if (plotType === 'histogram') {
    code += `fig <- plot_ly(x = ~${dataset}$${xVar},\n`;
    code += `               type = 'histogram',\n`;
    code += `               marker = list(color = 'steelblue',\n`;
    code += `                           line = list(color = 'white', width = 1)))`;
    
  } else if (plotType === 'bar') {
    code += `# First, summarize the data\n`;
    code += `library(dplyr)\n`;
    code += `summary_data <- ${dataset} %>%\n`;
    code += `  group_by(${colorVar !== 'none' ? colorVar : xVar}) %>%\n`;
    code += `  summarise(mean_val = mean(${yVar}, na.rm = TRUE))\n\n`;
    code += `fig <- plot_ly(data = summary_data,\n`;
    code += `               x = ~${colorVar !== 'none' ? colorVar : xVar},\n`;
    code += `               y = ~mean_val,\n`;
    code += `               type = 'bar')`;
    
  } else if (plotType === 'line') {
    code += `fig <- plot_ly(data = ${dataset},\n`;
    code += `               x = ~${xVar},\n`;
    code += `               y = ~${yVar},\n`;
    if (colorVar !== 'none') {
      code += `               color = ~${colorVar},\n`;
    }
    code += `               type = 'scatter',\n`;
    code += `               mode = 'lines+markers',\n`;
    code += `               line = list(width = 2))`;
    
  } else if (plotType === 'violin') {
    code += `fig <- plot_ly(data = ${dataset},\n`;
    code += `               x = ~${colorVar !== 'none' ? colorVar : xVar},\n`;
    code += `               y = ~${yVar},\n`;
    if (colorVar !== 'none') {
      code += `               color = ~${colorVar},\n`;
    }
    code += `               type = 'violin',\n`;
    code += `               box = list(visible = TRUE),\n`;
    code += `               meanline = list(visible = TRUE))`;
    
  } else if (plotType === 'heatmap') {
    code += `# Create correlation matrix\n`;
    code += `${dataset}_numeric <- ${dataset} %>% select(where(is.numeric))\n`;
    code += `cor_matrix <- cor(${dataset}_numeric, use = "complete.obs")\n\n`;
    code += `fig <- plot_ly(\n`;
    code += `  x = colnames(cor_matrix),\n`;
    code += `  y = rownames(cor_matrix),\n`;
    code += `  z = cor_matrix,\n`;
    code += `  type = "heatmap",\n`;
    code += `  colors = colorRamp(c("blue", "white", "red")))`;
    
  } else if (plotType === '3d') {
    code += `fig <- plot_ly(data = ${dataset},\n`;
    code += `               x = ~${xVar},\n`;
    code += `               y = ~${yVar},\n`;
    code += `               z = ~${xVar === 'Sepal.Length' ? 'Petal.Width' : 'Sepal.Width'},\n`;
    if (colorVar !== 'none') {
      code += `               color = ~${colorVar},\n`;
    }
    code += `               type = 'scatter3d',\n`;
    code += `               mode = 'markers',\n`;
    code += `               marker = list(size = 5))`;
  }
  
  // Add layout
  if (addTitle) {
    code += `\n\nfig <- fig %>% layout(\n`;
    code += `  title = "${plotType.charAt(0).toUpperCase() + plotType.slice(1)} Plot of ${dataset}",\n`;
    code += `  xaxis = list(title = "${xVar}"),\n`;
    code += `  yaxis = list(title = "${yVar}")\n`;
    code += `)`;
  }
  
  code += `\n\nfig`;
  
  document.getElementById('plotly-generated-code').textContent = code;
}

// Event listeners
document.getElementById('plotly-dataset').addEventListener('change', updatePlotlyVariableOptions);
document.getElementById('generate-plotly-code').addEventListener('click', generatePlotlyCode);

document.getElementById('copy-plotly-code').addEventListener('click', function() {
  const code = document.getElementById('plotly-generated-code').textContent;
  navigator.clipboard.writeText(code).then(() => {
    this.textContent = '✓ Copied!';
    setTimeout(() => {
      this.textContent = '📋 Copy';
    }, 2000);
  }).catch(err => {
    alert('Failed to copy code');
  });
});

// Initialize
updatePlotlyVariableOptions();
</script>
```

# Part 8: Best Practices

---

## When to Use Plotly 🤔

::: {.callout-note icon="false"}
**Choosing the Right Tool**
:::

**Choose Plotly for:**

✅ Interactive dashboards and web apps  
✅ Exploratory data analysis  
✅ Presentations where you can click and zoom  
✅ Sharing HTML reports  
✅ 3D visualizations

---

## When to Use ggplot2 🤔

::: {.callout-note icon="false"}
**Choose a static plot when publication control matters most.**
:::

✅ Publication-quality static graphics  
✅ Fine-grained control over every element  
✅ Complex multi-layered plots  
✅ PDF/PNG exports for papers  
✅ Faceted plots with many panels

**Need both?** Convert a ggplot with `ggplotly()`.

---

## Converting ggplot2 to Plotly 🔄 {.smaller}

::: {.callout-blue icon="false"}
**The Power of ggplotly()**
:::

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false
library(ggplot2)
library(plotly)

# Create a ggplot
p <- ggplot(iris, aes(x = Sepal.Length, y = Petal.Length, 
                     color = Species)) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Iris Dataset",
       x = "Sepal Length (cm)",
       y = "Petal Length (cm)")

# Convert to interactive Plotly plot
ggplotly(p)
```

**Advantages:**

- Keeps all your ggplot2 customization
- Automatically adds interactivity
- One line of code!

---

## Performance Tips 🚀

::: {.callout-warning icon="true"}
**Making Plotly Fast**
:::

**For Large Datasets:**

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false
# 1. Use webgl for better performance
fig <- plot_ly(data = large_dataset,
               x = ~x, y = ~y,
               type = 'scattergl',  # Note: scattergl instead of scatter
               mode = 'markers')

# 2. Reduce marker count with sampling
sampled <- large_dataset %>% sample_n(1000)
fig <- plot_ly(data = sampled, ...)

# 3. Disable hover for thousands of points
fig <- plot_ly(..., hoverinfo = 'skip')
```

---

## Keep Large Plots Responsive ⚡

::: {.callout-note icon="false"}
Choose a rendering strategy that matches the size of your data.
:::

**Tips:**

- Use `scattergl` for >1000 points
- Consider aggregation or binning for huge datasets
- Disable unnecessary interactive features

---

## Saving Plotly Plots 💾

::: {.callout-tip icon="true"}
**Export Options**
:::

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false
library(plotly)
library(htmlwidgets)

# Create a plot
fig <- plot_ly(iris, x = ~Sepal.Length, y = ~Petal.Length,
               color = ~Species, type = 'scatter', mode = 'markers')

# Save as interactive HTML
htmlwidgets::saveWidget(fig, "my_plot.html")
```

---

## Export a Static Image 🖼️

::: {.callout-tip icon="true"}
Static PNG export requires a configured image engine such as Kaleido.
:::

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false
# install.packages("reticulate")
# reticulate::py_install("kaleido")
library(orca)
orca(fig, "my_plot.png")
```

## Embed a Plot in a Report 📄

In an R Markdown or Quarto document, print the plot object to include it.
:::

```r
fig
```

## Key Takeaways: Core Ideas 🎯

::: {.callout-note icon="false"}
**What We Learned**
:::

**1. Installation:** Use `install.packages('plotly')` and setup functions

**2. Basic Syntax:**
```r
plot_ly(data = df, x = ~var1, y = ~var2, type = 'scatter')
```

**3. Plot Types:**
- Scatter, Box, Histogram, Bar, Line, Violin, Heatmap, 3D

**4. Binwidths:**
- Too few bins → lose detail
- Too many bins → too noisy
- Use Plotly's smart defaults or calculate optimal bins

---

::: {.callout-note icon="false"}
**Make plots clearer and shareable**
:::

**5. Customization:**
- `layout()` for axes, titles, colors
- `add_trace()` for multiple layers
- Annotations and shapes for context
